sentences.text: The Substation Field Crew is known operationally as Cinder during field activities.
Cinder performs inspections, maintenance, and switching support within the boundaries of approved work.
Field access begins only after the required work authorization and site entry controls are confirmed.
The Control Room Operator coordinates operational access with the Switching Desk Coordinator before work that could affect energized equipment.
The Substation Supervisor confirms that the requested work is consistent with current operating conditions and approved procedures.
The crew reviews the work scope, access route, known hazards, and communication arrangements before entering the yard.
Personnel use the site access process to record arrival and departure so that the control room can account for field staff.
Work boundaries are established before tools or test equipment are brought near electrical apparatus.
The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the applicable switching and clearance arrangements before work begins.
The Control Room Operator retains authority to suspend work when operating conditions change or indications become uncertain.
The Substation Field Crew verifies equipment identity at the point of work against the approved work documentation.
Field personnel do not rely on screen indications alone to establish that equipment is safe to approach or handle.
Required checks of position, isolation, and absence of hazardous energy are performed using approved site procedures.
Any discrepancy between field observations and control-room indications is treated as an unsafe condition until resolved.
The crew promptly reports uncertain equipment conditions through the designated operational communication channel.
Substation Field Crew completes and sends the Breaker Inspection Tag after recording the observed breaker condition and inspection time.
The Station Supervisory Control System presents available equipment indications for operator review during normal operation.
The Bay Automation Controller applies configured permissives and interlocks to supported automated operations.
Automation does not replace field verification when a procedure requires direct confirmation of equipment condition.
The Control Room Operator evaluates reported field conditions before authorizing a return to automated operation.
Field crews maintain communications with the control room throughout work that could affect protection, control, or service continuity.
If communications are lost, the crew stops affected work and follows the approved hold and escalation procedure.
Work is considered complete only after personnel, tools, and temporary connections are accounted for and the work area is left in a safe state.
The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the operational handback arrangements before equipment is returned to service.
